subject: Biology
summary: According to the WHO, reproductive health implies total physical, emotional, behavioral, and social well-being in all aspects of reproduction. Covers Family Planning, RCH, Saheli, Amniocentesis & PCPNDT Act, Comprehensive Contraceptive Modalities, MTP Act & RU-486, STIs/RTIs taxonomy, and Assisted Reproductive Technologies (IVF, ZIFT, IUT, GIFT, ICSI, IUI).

sections.title: Reproductive Health Imperatives, RCH Programs, & Saheli
sections.topic: WHO Health Definition, RCH Objectives, MMR/IMR, & CDRI Saheli Formulation

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: WHO definition: Reproductive health implies total physical, emotional, behavioral, and social well-being. 1951: India became the FIRST country globally to launch a national Family Planning program, later expanded into RCH. CDRI Lucknow developed Saheli (Centchroman / Ormeloxifene), a non-steroidal once-a-week oral contraceptive pill.

sections.codeSnippet:
NATIONAL REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH TIMELINE
                                      │
  1951: India becomes FIRST country globally to launch national **Family Planning Program**.
                                      │
  1990s: Program expanded into **Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH)** program.
                                      │
  CDRI Lucknow Innovation: Developed **Saheli** (Centchroman / Ormeloxifene), a non-steroidal
  once-a-week oral contraceptive pill with high efficiency and minimal side-effects.
sections.content:
### 1.1 National Reproductive Health Initiatives
- **1951 (Family Planning Program)**: India was the first country globally to launch a national Family Planning Program.
- **Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH)**: Aims at creating awareness regarding reproductive processes, providing medical care, and reducing Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) and Infant Mortality Rate (IMR).
- **Saheli (Centchroman / Ormeloxifene)**: Developed by CDRI Lucknow. A non-steroidal Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM), taken once-a-week with minimal side effects.

sections.title: Amniocentesis, Prenatal Diagnostics, & The PCPNDT Act
sections.topic: Amniocentesis Protocol (14-16w), Fetal Karyotyping, Inborn Metabolic Errors, & PCPNDT Legal Ban

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Amniocentesis (14–16 weeks gestation) extracts amniotic fluid for fetal karyotyping (Down, Turner, Klinefelter) and inborn metabolic error detection (PKU, Sickle Cell). PCPNDT Act (1994) statutorily bans prenatal sex determination to eliminate female foeticide.

sections.codeSnippet:
AMNIOCENTESIS PROCEDURE FLOW
                        
   Ultrasound-guided transabdominal needle insertion into Amniotic Sac
                                     │
   Withdrawal of ~10-20 mL Amniotic Fluid (contains fetal skin/epithelial cells)
                                     │
   Centrifugation ──► Cultured Fetal Cells ──► Karyotyping & Enzymatic Assays
sections.content:
### 2.1 Amniocentesis & PCPNDT Act (1994)
- **Diagnostic Scope**: Detects chromosomal aneuploidies (Down Syndrome 47,+21; Turner 45,X0; Klinefelter 47,XXY) and inborn metabolic errors (PKU, Sickle Cell Anemia, Albinism).
- **PCPNDT Act (1994)**: Statutorily prohibits using prenatal diagnostics for fetal sex determination, with severe legal penalties to eradicate female foeticide.

sections.title: Population Demographics, Natural, & Barrier Contraceptive Methods
sections.topic: Demographic Explosion Drivers, Periodic Abstinence, LAM, & Condoms/Diaphragms

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Population drivers: drop in death rate, MMR, and IMR with expanded reproductive age cohort. Natural methods: Periodic abstinence (Days 10–17), Coitus interruptus, and LAM (up to 6 months). Barrier methods: Condoms (only method protecting against STIs/HIV) and Diaphragms/Caps with Nonoxynol-9 spermicides.

sections.codeSnippet:
CONTRACEPTIVE MODALITIES
                                         │
     ┌──────────────┬────────────┼────────────┼────────────┬─────────────┐
     ▼              ▼            ▼            ▼            ▼             ▼
  NATURAL        BARRIER        IUDs        ORAL PILLS    INJECTABLE    SURGICAL
  ├── Rhythm     ├── Condoms  ├── Non-Med  ├── Daily      ├── Norplant ├── Vasectomy
  ├── Coitus Int ├── Diaphragm├── Copper   └── **Saheli** └── Depo-Provera└── Tubectomy
  └── LAM        └── Vaults   └── Hormone      (Weekly)
sections.content:
### 3.1 Contraceptive Modalities Overview
- **Periodic Abstinence**: Avoid coitus during fertile window (Days 10–17).
- **Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM)**: Prolactin-induced ovulation suppression (up to 6 months).
- **Condoms (e.g. Nirodh)**: Protects against both unwanted pregnancy and STIs/HIV.

sections.title: Intrauterine Devices (IUDs) & Copper-Releasing Biochemical Mechanisms

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: IUD classes: Non-medicated (Lippes Loop: macrophage phagocytosis), Copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375: Cu2+ suppresses sperm motility/viability), and Hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20: atrophic endometrium & thick cervical mucus plug).

sections.codeSnippet:
IUD CATEGORIES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
  NON-MEDICATED IUDs            COPPER-RELEASING IUDs         HORMONE-RELEASING IUDs
  ├── Lippes Loop               ├── CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375   ├── Progestasert, LNG-20
  └── Attracts macrophages;     └── Suppresses sperm motility └── Makes uterus unsuitable for
      increases phagocytosis        & fertilizing capacity       implantation & cervix thick
sections.content:
### 4.1 Intrauterine Device Taxonomy
- **Copper-Releasing IUDs**: Free Cu2+ suppresses sperm motility and inhibits acrosomal enzymes (hyaluronidase/acrosin).
- **Hormone-Releasing IUDs**: Levonorgestrel renders the endometrium hostile to implantation and creates a thick cervical mucus plug.

sections.title: Oral Contraceptive Pills, Hormonal Implants, & Emergency Contraception
sections.topic: Daily Combined Pills (21+7), Norplant Subdermal Implants, & Levonorgestrel Emergency Window

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Daily pills (21 + 7 iron) contain synthetic Progestogen + Estrogen combinations, abolishing the LH surge and inhibiting ovulation. Subdermal implants (Norplant, 5 years). Emergency contraception: Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg within 72 hours of unprotected coitus.

sections.codeSnippet:
HORMONAL CONTRACEPTIVE MECHANISMS
                                  │
  ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
  ▼                               ▼                               ▼
OVULATION INHIBITION        CERVICAL MUCUS THICKENING       ENDOMETRIAL HOSTILITY
Negative feedback on        Thickens cervical plug to       Inhibits proliferation,
pituitary LH/FSH surge.     prevent sperm entry into uterus.preventing blastocyst implantation.
sections.content:
### 5.1 Hormonal Contraception
- **Combined Pills**: Inhibit ovulation via negative feedback on GnRH and LH/FSH.
- **Norplant / Implanon**: Subdermal levonorgestrel rods providing 5-year contraception.
- **Emergency Contraception**: High-dose progestogens (1.5 mg LNG) within 72 hours of coitus.

sections.title: Surgical Sterilization: Vasectomy & Tubectomy Mechanics
sections.topic: Terminal Sterilization Techniques, Azoospermic Semen, & Normal Ovarian Cycles

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Surgical sterilization (>99% efficacy, poor reversibility): Vasectomy (scrotal incision, vas deferens severed, testosterone & semen volume normal, azoospermic) vs Tubectomy (abdominal/vaginal incision, Fallopian tubes severed, ovulation & menses normal).

sections.codeSnippet:
STERILIZATION METHOD COMPARISON
                       
      VASECTOMY (Male Sterilization)              TUBECTOMY (Female Sterilization)
      ├── Small incision in Scrotum              ├── Small incision in Abdomen / Vagina
      ├── Section of Vas Deferens cut & tied     ├── Section of Fallopian Tubes cut & tied
      ├── Does NOT affect Testosterone           ├── Does NOT affect Menstrual Cycle
      └── Semen volume normal, but LACKS sperm   └── Prevents sperm-egg meeting
sections.content:
### 6.1 Vasectomy & Tubectomy
- **Vasectomy**: Severing of vasa deferentia. Testosterone and semen volume remain unaffected; ejaculate is completely azoospermic.
- **Tubectomy**: Severing of Fallopian tubes. Ovulation and menstrual cycles continue normally.

sections.title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) & RU-486 Pharmacodynamics
sections.topic: MTP Act 1971 / 2021 Legal Thresholds & Mifepristone-Misoprostol Dual Regimen

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: MTP (induced abortion, ~45–50 million/year globally). MTP Amendment Act: ≤12 weeks requires 1 RMP; 12–24 weeks requires 2 RMPs. Medical abortion: Mifepristone (RU-486, progesterone receptor antagonist) followed by Misoprostol (PGE1 analog, uterine contractions).

sections.codeSnippet:
MTP ACT LEGAL AMENDMENTS (INDIA)
                      
   MTP Act 1971 (Legalized to prevent maternal mortality from illegal unsafe abortions).
                                     │
   MTP Amendment Act (2017 / 2021):
   ├── Up to 12 Weeks Gestation (1st Trimester) ──► Requires opinion of ONE RMP.
   └── 12 to 24 Weeks Gestation (2nd Trimester) ──► Requires opinion of TWO RMPs.
sections.content:
### 7.1 MTP Legal Rules & Mifepristone Dual Regimen
- **MTP Thresholds**: 1 RMP (up to 12 weeks), 2 RMPs (12–24 weeks).
- **Mifepristone (RU-486)**: Progesterone receptor blocker causing decidual detachment.
- **Misoprostol**: Prostaglandin E1 analog inducing strong myometrial contractions and cervical dilation.

sections.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) & Pathogen Matrix
sections.topic: Bacterial, Viral, & Protozoan STIs, Incurable Viral Spectrum, & PID Complications

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: STIs / RTIs: Bacterial (Syphilis - Treponema, Gonorrhea - Neisseria, Chlamydiasis - Chlamydia: all CURABLE), Viral (AIDS - HIV, Hepatitis B - HBV, Genital Herpes - HSV-2: all INCURABLE), Protozoan (Trichomoniasis: CURABLE). Complications: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID), ectopic pregnancy, cervical carcinoma, infertility.

sections.codeSnippet:
PATHOGENIC CLASSES OF STIs
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                                 ▼                                 ▼
BACTERIAL STIs                    VIRAL STIs                     PROTOZOAN / FUNGAL
├── Syphilis (Treponema)          ├── AIDS (HIV Retrovirus)      ├── Trichomoniasis (Trichomonas)
├── Gonorrhea (Neisseria)         ├── Hepatitis B (HBV)          └── Candidiasis (Candida)
└── Chlamydiasis (Chlamydia)      └── Genital Herpes (HSV-2)
sections.content:
### 8.1 STI Spectrum & Curability
- **Curable STIs**: Syphilis (Penicillin), Gonorrhea (Ceftriaxone), Chlamydia (Azithromycin), Trichomoniasis (Metronidazole).
- **Incurable Viral STIs**: HIV/AIDS, Hepatitis B, Genital Herpes (HSV-2), HPV.
- **Complications**: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID), tubal blockage, ectopic gestation, and infertility.

sections.title: In-Vitro Fertilization (IVF), ZIFT, & IUT Protocols
sections.topic: IVF-ET Workflow, ZIFT (≤8 Blastomeres to Tube), & IUT (>8 Blastomeres to Uterus)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Infertility is the inability to conceive after 2 years unprotected coitus. IVF: fertilization outside body in culture dish. Embryo transfer (ET): ZIFT (early embryo ≤8 blastomeres to Fallopian tube) vs IUT (advanced embryo >8 blastomeres directly into Uterine cavity).

sections.codeSnippet:
ASSISTED REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGIES (ART)
                                           │
         ┌─────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                                   ▼
   IN-VITRO FERTILIZATION (IVF)                                        IN-VIVO FERTILIZATION
   (Fertilization OUTSIDE body in glass dish)                         (Fertilization INSIDE female tract)
   ├── ZIFT (Zygote Transfer <= 8 Blastomeres to Tube)                 ├── GIFT (Gamete Transfer to Tube)
   └── IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer > 8 Blastomeres)                   ├── ICSI (Micro-injection into Ovum)
                                                                      └── IUI / AI (Artificial Insemination)
sections.content:
### 9.1 In-Vitro ART: ZIFT vs. IUT
- **ZIFT**: Embryo containing $\le 8$ blastomeres transferred into the Fallopian tube.
- **IUT**: Embryo containing $> 8$ blastomeres (16–32 cells) transferred directly into the uterus.

sections.title: In-Vivo ART Modalities: GIFT, ICSI, & IUI Insemination
sections.topic: GIFT (Gamete Transfer), ICSI (Micromanipulation for Oligospermia), & IUI (Uterine Insemination)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer): unfertilized ovum and sperm placed in Fallopian tube for in-vivo fertilization. ICSI (Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection): single selected sperm injected directly into ovum cytoplasm for severe male oligospermia. IUI / AI: washed motile sperm injected into uterine cavity.

sections.codeSnippet:
IN-VIVO ART MODALITIES MATRIX
                      
   GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer)
   ├── Unfertilized Ovum + Sperm transferred into Fallopian Tube.
   └── Indication: Female cannot produce ova, but provides suitable tube/uterine environment.
   
   ICSI (Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection)
   ├── Single sperm injected directly into Ovum cytoplasm using a micropipette.
   └── Indication: Severe male factor infertility (oligospermia / asthenozoospermia).
   
   IUI (Intra-Uterine Insemination) / AI
   ├── Processed high-motility semen injected directly into Uterine cavity.
   └── Indication: Male partner has low sperm count or inability to inseminate.
sections.content:
### 10.1 In-Vivo and Micromanipulation ART
- **GIFT**: In-vivo fertilization inside recipient's Fallopian tube for female ovulatory failure.
- **ICSI**: Direct microinjection of single sperm into oocyte for severe oligospermia ($<2\text{ million/mL}$).
- **IUI / AI**: Washed sperm injected into uterine cavity during ovulation window.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Master reproductive health glossary with 30+ definitions and 10 high-yield NEST misconceptions.

sections.content:
### 11.1 Master Glossary & NEST Traps
- **ZIFT vs IUT Blastomere Cutoff**: $\le 8$ cells (ZIFT) vs $> 8$ cells (IUT).
- **Saheli**: Non-steroidal once-a-week oral SERM pill.
- **PCPNDT Act**: Statutory ban on prenatal sex determination to eliminate female foeticide.
- **Incurable Viral STIs**: HIV, Hepatitis B, and Genital Herpes (HSV-2).
